nodes.title: Three-stage classifiers and access-dependent fallback
nodes.statement: All traffic is screened by an activation probe; flagged cyber traffic goes to an Opus 5.5 lightweight classifier, then potentially violative traffic to a separate trained LLM classifier used with the probe verdict. Training data were augmented with jailbreaks and automated attacks and weighted toward long agentic tasks. Source-code vulnerability discovery is allowed; compiled-binary discovery blocked. A temporarily wider margin is described. Cyber blocks fall back to Opus 4.8 automatically in Anthropic applications; API developers must opt in; provider behaviour may differ. CVP access is prospective.
nodes.quote: This happens automatically in our own applications; on the API, the developer must opt in to automatic fallbacks.

nodes.title: User-pasted instruction weakness and product mitigation
nodes.statement: Earlier snapshot followed planted instructions in 52% of simulated attempts; a pre-release invisible-character test had 18/68. With product mitigations, no visible/invisible planted instructions were followed in reported tests. Tool-result version had 0/105.

nodes.title: Coverage and actual release operation
nodes.statement: The public record describes a three-stage pipeline, temporary wider margin and aggregate coverage, but does not expose an auditable end-to-end mapping of deployed classifier versions, per-stage errors, threat-stratum coverage and release-interface operation. Product mitigation tests do not by themselves establish deployment coverage.
nodes.public_evidence_observation: The public record describes a three-stage pipeline, temporary wider margin and aggregate coverage, but does not expose an auditable end-to-end mapping of deployed classifier versions, per-stage errors, threat-stratum coverage and release-interface operation. Product mitigation tests do not by themselves establish deployment coverage.
nodes.why_material: The root includes policy enforcement in general access; aggregate recall and deployment descriptions leave a bridge to what a user actually receives.
nodes.evidence_needed_for_closure: A dated release configuration matrix by interface/access tier; policy-labelled representative evaluation set or audited aggregate strata with denominators, stage and end-to-end false-negative/false-positive estimates and uncertainty; evidence of routing/block operation and release rollout of relevant product mitigations; a change/monitoring summary would narrow ongoing-operation inference.
nodes.absence_or_redaction_reason: MIXED: §3.4.2 explicitly uses aggregation preserving user privacy. Reason for undisclosed classifier thresholds, sample details or deployment logs is UNKNOWN_REASON; no blanket deliberate-redaction inference.
nodes.applicability: General-access Opus 5.5, 22 September release. CVP is prospective; API opt-in and provider differences persist. Pasted-text tests have their own threat model.
nodes.run_quality_weakness: Coverage sample sizes, repeated runs and uncertainty are not quantified here; no graph-derived chart values or invented denominators.
nodes.counterargument_or_alternative_taxonomy: The figures and architecture do provide evidence. Safe aggregate disclosure or independent audit could narrow the link without releasing harmful examples. One could split measurement coverage from operational deployment; ARGUS groups them as policy-enforcement warrant.
nodes.private_evidence_non_inference: Not located or not reported in this bounded public corpus does not mean nonexistent internally, ineffective control, misconduct, or known harm. Closure requests are proposed evidence, not assertions that such evidence exists.

nodes.why_material: Without that bridge a reader cannot audit how adverse findings qualify the reported robustness or why they were not classified critical.

nodes.absence_or_redaction_reason: UNKNOWN_REASON for missing adjudication/transcripts/comparison detail; no explicit source-specific redaction rationale located.

nodes.title: Composite fallback and surface-specific generalization
nodes.statement: Static fallback rollouts had no successful attacks, while adaptive coding successes were fallback-served even with probes. GUI included direct-model successes. Pasted-user-text and browser configurations differ. No single public experiment validates all release combinations or a shared acceptable composite failure criterion.
nodes.public_evidence_observation: Static fallback rollouts had no successful attacks, while adaptive coding successes were fallback-served even with probes. GUI included direct-model successes. Pasted-user-text and browser configurations differ. No single public experiment validates all release combinations or a shared acceptable composite failure criterion.
nodes.why_material: Model-only zero observations cannot support a blanket interpretation of deployed-system robustness; routing can move a request to a different susceptibility.
nodes.evidence_needed_for_closure: End-to-end evaluation by interface, access setting, model/classifier/fallback version and product protection; per-routing-path valid-response denominators and outcome intervals; adaptive tests spanning coding, GUI, browser and pasted-text threats; documented acceptance rationale and mitigation retests for fallback-served failures.
nodes.absence_or_redaction_reason: UNKNOWN_REASON for unavailable deployment matrix, logs and complete composite acceptance evidence. The adverse results themselves are public, not hidden.
nodes.applicability: General access composite behaviour only. First-party automatic fallback; API opt-in; providers may differ. Prompt-injection results are a relevant deployment dependency, not automatically cyber-jailbreak critical-severity findings.
nodes.run_quality_weakness: Attempt budgets, valid responses, scenarios and fallback rollouts differ; no pooling ASRs across static/adaptive tests or inferring deployment incident rates.
nodes.counterargument_or_alternative_taxonomy: Adaptive attacker access is deliberately permissive and probe protection sharply reduces coding ASR. Browser auto mode reports zero in its test. An alternative taxonomy separates offensive misuse prevention from protection of users against injection; that split does not remove fallback applicability.
nodes.private_evidence_non_inference: Not located or not reported in this bounded public corpus does not mean nonexistent internally, ineffective control, misconduct, or known harm. Closure requests are proposed evidence, not assertions that such evidence exists.
